newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on flood forecasts, soy rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on flood forecasts, soy rally.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on concerns about forecasts for spring flooding in the U.S. Midwest with a late rally in soybeans and soymeal also cited, traders said.
"The flooding worries are a very real concern. But the sooner it floods and gets it out of the way the sooner they can plant (spring wheat)," a trader said.

Traders said the wheat market was caught between bullish influence from the potential flooding this spring in the U.S. Northern Midwest spring wheat growing region and bearish input from ongoing signs of strong competition for wheat exports.

Traders said there was more incentive to purchase wheat futures now that the March was off the board and also pointed to the net short position of funds in wheat as a scenario allowing more room for wheat to move to the upside.
CBOT March wheat expired Wednesday at 1201 CST. The March went off the board one cent higher at $3.78.
Wheat closed 7-3/4 cents per bushel higher to one cent lower, with May up 7-1/4 at $3.91.
There was a potpourri of wheat news circulating but the market lacked direction until late dealings and was dominated by positioning before the March contract expired.
Canadian Wheat Board chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said Tuesday the Canadian wheat and durum sales to processors in the United States are not distorting the U.S. wheat market.
Also Tuesday plant pathologists said current levels of leaf rust fungus in southern U.S. Plains wheat may foreshadow significant yield reduction in the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop.
Technicians early Wednesday cited first support in the May at $3.80 and second support at $3.74. The session low for May was $3.82-1/2.
First resistance in the May was $3.86 and second resistance was at $3.92. The session high for May was $3.92.
The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Tuesday.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the May closed at 68.7 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

Prudential Securities, Iowa Grain and Refco Inc each bought one million bushels of July, traders said. Tenco Inc, LFG Futures, Griffin Trading, The Chicago Corp and Cargill Investor Services each sold small volumes of the July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 13,000, below the 14,126 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 300 July $3.60 calls and sold 300 July $4.00 calls at 16 cents, traders said. Rand Financial bought 100 July $4.60 calls and sold 100 July $4.30 calls at three cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, above the 2,463 traded Tuesday.
